question: Which of the following is a tip the Alabama CDL Manual gives for avoiding becoming a distracted driver?
choice_a: Turn off all communication devices
choice_b: Type text messages only while stopped at red lights
choice_c: Review maps and program the GPS while driving
choice_d: Keep the interior cab light on for visibility
explanation: The manual lists 'Turn off all communication devices' as a tip to avoid distraction, and separately instructs drivers not to type or read text messages while driving and to review maps and program GPS before starting the trip.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-23

question: What does the manual recommend doing first when confronted by an aggressive driver?
choice_a: Speed up to hold your position in the lane
choice_b: Make every attempt to get out of their way
choice_c: Flash your high beams to signal your displeasure
choice_d: Follow closely behind them to discourage further aggression
explanation: The manual states, 'First and foremost, make every attempt to get out of their way,' when confronted by an aggressive driver.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-24

question: Why does the manual advise against wearing dark or tinted corrective lenses at night?
choice_a: They are more likely to shatter than clear lenses
choice_b: They cut down the light needed to see clearly under night driving conditions
choice_c: They are prohibited by federal regulation for all drivers
choice_d: They increase the glare produced by oncoming headlights
explanation: The manual states that tinted lenses 'cut down the light that you need to see clearly under night driving conditions,' even if a driver thinks they help with glare.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-24

question: Per the manual, roughly how far will a vehicle traveling 55 mph travel during just two seconds of glare blindness?
choice_a: A few feet
choice_b: About one car length
choice_c: More than half the distance of a football field
choice_d: Less than 10 yards
explanation: The manual states a vehicle going 55 mph will travel more than half the distance of a football field during the time it takes to recover from glare blindness.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-25

question: About how far ahead can a driver see when using low-beam headlights at night, according to the manual?
choice_a: 100 feet
choice_b: 250 feet
choice_c: 500 feet
choice_d: 700 feet
explanation: The manual states, 'With low beams you can see ahead about 250 feet and with high beams about 350-500 feet.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-27

question: According to the National Sleep Foundation poll cited in the manual, what percentage of Americans admit to having actually fallen asleep at the wheel in the past year?
explanation: The manual cites the poll finding that 'more than one third (36 percent or 103 million people) admit to having actually fallen asleep at the wheel.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-25

question: According to the manual, working more than 60 hours a week increases a driver's risk of a drowsy-driving crash by what percentage?
explanation: The manual lists 'Working more than 60 hours a week (increases your risk by 40%)' as a fatigue risk factor to consider before driving.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-26

question: What is the manual's best advice for driving in fog?
choice_a: Increase your speed to clear the fog area quickly
choice_b: Follow closely behind another vehicle's taillights
choice_c: Don't drive; pull off the road until visibility improves
choice_d: Use high-beam headlights for maximum visibility
explanation: The manual states, 'The best advice for driving in fog is don't. It is preferable that you pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility is better.' It also specifically recommends low-beam (not high-beam) headlights if you must drive.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-28

question: What is the minimum tread depth required in every major groove on front tires, according to the manual?
choice_a: 2/32 inch
choice_b: 4/32 inch
choice_c: 6/32 inch
choice_d: 8/32 inch
explanation: The manual requires 'at least 4/32 inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires and at least 2/32 inch on other tires' (2/32 inch applies to the other tires, not the front tires).
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-29

question: What does a lack of spray from other vehicles on a wet road most likely indicate, per the manual?
choice_a: The road has recently been repaved
choice_b: Ice has formed on the road
choice_c: Other drivers are being overly cautious
choice_d: The road temperature is well above freezing
explanation: The manual states, 'A lack of spray from other vehicles indicates ice has formed on the road,' as part of checking for ice while driving in winter.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-30

question: When driving in very hot weather, how often does the manual recommend inspecting your tires?
choice_a: Every 500 miles or once a day
choice_b: Every two hours or every 100 miles
choice_c: Only before starting the trip
choice_d: Every 1,000 miles
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to 'Inspect the tires every two hours or every 100 miles when driving in very hot weather,' since air pressure increases with temperature.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-30

question: What distinguishes a 'passive' railroad-highway crossing from an 'active' one, according to the manual?
choice_a: Passive crossings have gates and flashing lights; active crossings do not
choice_b: Passive crossings have no traffic control device, while active crossings have devices such as flashing lights or gates
choice_c: Passive crossings are found only on private property
choice_d: There is no real difference between the two terms
explanation: The manual defines a passive crossing as one that 'does not have any type of traffic control device,' leaving the decision to stop or proceed to the driver, while active crossings 'have a traffic control device installed... to regulate traffic,' such as flashing red lights and gates.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-30

question: About how long does it take a typical tractor-trailer unit to clear a single railroad track, per the manual?
choice_a: 5 seconds
choice_b: 14 seconds
choice_c: 25 seconds
choice_d: 40 seconds
explanation: The manual states, 'It takes a typical tractor-trailer unit at least 14 seconds to clear a single track and more than 15 seconds to clear a double track.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-31

question: What does the manual say should be used as the principal way of controlling vehicle speed on a long, steep downgrade?
choice_a: The parking brake
choice_b: The braking effect of the engine
choice_c: Repeated hard application of the service brakes
choice_d: Rapid downshifting while already moving fast
explanation: The manual states, 'You must use the braking effect of the engine as the principal way of controlling your speed,' saving the brakes so they are available when needed for stopping.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-32

question: What happens to brakes that are used too much on a long downgrade and become excessively hot, per the manual?
choice_a: They become more responsive to pedal pressure
choice_b: They may 'fade,' requiring harder and harder application to get the same stopping power
choice_c: They automatically disengage for safety
choice_d: Heat has no effect on brake performance
explanation: The manual explains that if brakes become too hot they may start to 'fade,' meaning the driver must apply them harder and harder, and if hard use continues, the brakes can keep fading until the vehicle cannot slow down or stop at all.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-32

question: In the manual's example of proper braking technique, if your 'safe' speed on a downgrade is 40 mph, at what speed should you release the brakes after applying them?
choice_a: 40 mph
choice_b: 38 mph
choice_c: 35 mph
choice_d: 30 mph
explanation: The manual's example says you apply the brakes hard enough to gradually reduce your speed from 40 mph to 35 mph (about 5 mph below your safe speed) and then release them, repeating as needed.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-33

question: Why does the manual suggest that steering away from an obstacle may be safer than braking in some emergencies?
choice_a: You can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
choice_b: Steering causes less tire wear than braking
choice_c: Braking is not permitted in emergency situations
choice_d: Steering automatically engages the antilock braking system
explanation: The manual states, 'Stopping is not always the safest thing to do in an emergency... you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-33

question: What is the 'stab braking' method for stopping quickly, as described in the manual?
choice_a: Applying the brakes gently and holding light, steady pressure
choice_b: Applying the brakes all the way, releasing when the wheels lock up, then reapplying fully once the wheels start rolling again
choice_c: Pumping the brake pedal rapidly in short, light taps
choice_d: Using only the parking brake to bring the vehicle to a stop
explanation: The manual describes stab braking as applying the brakes all the way, releasing when the wheels lock up, and reapplying the brakes fully as soon as the wheels start rolling again.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-34

question: What does the manual warn may happen to the steering wheel if a front tire fails while driving?
choice_a: It can be twisted out of your hand if you are not gripping it firmly with both hands
choice_b: It will automatically lock in place
choice_c: It has no effect on the steering wheel at all
choice_d: Only rear tire failures affect the steering wheel
explanation: The manual states, 'If a front tire fails, it can twist the steering wheel out of your hand. The only way to prevent this is to keep a firm grip on the steering wheel with both hands at all times.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-35

question: According to the manual, what does an Antilock Braking System (ABS) actually do?
choice_a: It increases your normal braking capability
choice_b: It decreases your normal braking capability for safety
choice_c: It keeps your wheels from locking up during hard braking, without changing your normal braking capability
choice_d: It guarantees a shorter stopping distance in every situation
explanation: The manual states ABS 'is an addition to your normal brakes. It does not decrease or increase your normal braking capability,' and that it 'does not necessarily shorten your stopping distance, but it does help you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-35

question: If the ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the bulb check or comes on while driving, what does the manual say you should do?
choice_a: Immediately stop and abandon the vehicle
choice_b: Recognize you may have lost ABS control on one or more wheels, drive and brake normally since your regular brakes still work, and get the system serviced soon
choice_c: Ignore it, since the ABS lamp has no functional meaning
choice_d: Disconnect the vehicle battery to reset the ABS system
explanation: The manual notes that if the lamp stays on you may have lost ABS control, but reminds drivers, 'you still have regular brakes. Drive normally, but get the system serviced soon.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-37

question: According to the manual, which of the following are the four causes of skids?
choice_a: Over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast for conditions
choice_b: Worn tires, bad weather, poor visibility, and mechanical failure only
choice_c: Excessive cargo weight, poor alignment, low fuel, and driver fatigue
choice_d: Only mechanical brake failure causes skids
explanation: The manual states a skid is caused by over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, or driving too fast for road conditions, noting that most serious skids result from driving too fast for conditions.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-36

question: What is the first thing you should do to correct a drive-wheel braking skid, per the manual?
choice_a: Apply the brakes even harder
choice_b: Stop braking, to let the rear wheels roll again
choice_c: Turn the steering wheel sharply in the direction of the skid
choice_d: Accelerate hard to regain traction
explanation: The manual's first step to correct a drive-wheel braking skid is 'Stop Braking. This will let the rear wheels roll again, and keep the rear wheels from sliding.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-37

question: What are the basic steps to be taken at any accident scene, according to the manual?
choice_a: Protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured
choice_b: Immediately move all involved vehicles before authorities arrive
choice_c: Leave the scene right away to avoid liability, then call police later
choice_d: Stay inside your vehicle and take no action until police arrive
explanation: The manual states, 'The basic steps to be taken at any accident are to: Protect the area. Notify authorities. Care for the injured.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-38

question: Why does the manual say you should keep the doors shut on a van or box trailer with a cargo fire?
choice_a: Opening the doors supplies the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn very fast
choice_b: Opening the doors has no effect on the fire
choice_c: Opening the doors automatically activates a built-in fire extinguisher
choice_d: It is only a concern if the cargo is refrigerated
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to keep the doors shut on a van or box trailer cargo fire, especially with hazardous materials, because 'Opening the van doors will supply the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn very fast.'
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-39

question: Per the manual's fire class chart, which extinguishing method should NOT be used on an electrical equipment fire (Class C)?
choice_a: Carbon dioxide
choice_b: Dry chemicals
choice_c: Water
choice_d: Non-conducting agents
explanation: The manual states electrical equipment fires should be extinguished 'with Non-conducting Agents such as Carbon Dioxide or Dry Chemicals. DO NOT USE WATER,' since water can cause shock on an electrical fire.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-39

question: According to the manual, approximately how much alcohol can the liver process per hour?
choice_a: One full standard drink
choice_b: One-third of an ounce
choice_c: Two full drinks
choice_d: The liver does not process alcohol
explanation: The manual states, 'The liver can only process one-third an ounce of alcohol per hour, which is considerably less than the alcohol in a standard drink,' which is why only time, not coffee or a cold shower, can sober a person up.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-40

question: As Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) builds up, which part of the brain does the manual say is affected first?
choice_a: The part controlling judgment and self-control
choice_b: The part controlling heart rate only
choice_c: The part controlling long-term memory
choice_d: No part of the brain is affected until BAC exceeds .15
explanation: The manual states, 'The first part of the brain affected controls judgment and self-control... good judgment and self-control are absolutely necessary for safe driving,' and this effect can keep drinkers from realizing they are getting drunk.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-40
